idea: a tiny C toy with a Makefile, to see how a fixed-timestep loop catches up after a stall
questions: What should visibly catch up after a stall — a moving dot, or just printed numbers?
Should the stall be a real clock sleep, and roughly how long should it last?
With 25 catch-up steps landing in one frame, should we cap steps per frame?
answers: printed numbers. one line per frame: frame, steps this frame, total steps
a real sleep of half a second, once, at frame 20. the sim steps at 50 Hz
no cap yet, I want to see all 25 land in one frame. the cap comes after

files.does: builds main.c and runs it when you type make run
50 Hz loop, one 0.5s sleep at frame 20, one line per frame

slice.shows: A line per frame: frame, steps, total. 20 quiet frames, one with 25 steps, then quiet.
probes: Move the sleep to frame 30: watch the big line move, still 25 steps
Make the sleep 0.1s: 5 steps land instead of 25
Run 100 frames instead of 40: totals keep pace with frames
Sleep twice: two big lines, both 25, total never lags frames
slice.test: 0.5s at 50 Hz is 25: assert that line shows 25 steps and the total tracks frames.
later: the cap on steps per frame
a moving dot or any drawing
timing stats or a frame-rate summary

makefile:
CC ?= cc
CFLAGS ?= -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -O2

run: main
	./main

main: main.c
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o main main.c

clean:
	rm -f main

.PHONY: run clean
makefileSaid: I wrote the Makefile: `make run` builds main.c with cc and runs it, plus a `clean` target — no tests were run. Note main.c doesn't exist yet, so `make run` will fail until we write it.
mainSaid: I wrote main.c: a 40-frame loop that paces each frame with a 20 ms sleep (500 ms at frame 20), adds the measured elapsed time to an accumulator and runs 50 Hz steps while it lasts, printing frame, steps and total. No tests ran; expect 1 step per frame except frame 20 at 25.
